h1: BMW Engine Matching by Registration & VIN
lede: We identify the correct engine specification for your BMW before any rebuild or replacement work begins - using your registration number and VIN.

blocks.html: Engine matching is the process of identifying the correct engine specification for a specific vehicle using its registration number and Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). It ensures every rebuild or replacement we carry out uses the correct components for your exact BMW.

items: **VIN decoding** - The 17-character VIN contains production date, model or chassis code, engine type, drivetrain information, and optional equipment.
**Registration lookup** - The V5C registration document records engine capacity and fuel type, which combined with the model and year usually confirms the engine family.
**Parts catalogue cross-reference** - The VIN is used to query manufacturer parts catalogues to identify the exact engine variant fitted to that specific vehicle.
**Component verification** - For absolute certainty, the physical engine number on the block is compared against the VIN record.

**Compatibility assessment** - If a replacement engine is being sourced, we confirm that the donor engine matches the recipient vehicle's specifications - same engine code, appropriate ancillaries, correct mounting points.

paras: Engine matching is included as part of our [engine rebuild](/bmw-engine-rebuild) or [engine replacement](/bmw-engine-replacement) service. We do not offer standalone engine matching without associated work.

items.q: Why is VIN matching important for a BMW engine rebuild?
items.a: VIN matching ensures we use the correct engine specification for your exact vehicle. BMW engines vary by model, year, and optional equipment - even the same engine code can have different ancillaries, sumps, and mounting points between chassis. Matching by VIN guarantees compatibility.

items.q: Can you match an engine for a BMW that's had a previous replacement?
items.a: Yes. We verify the current engine number against the VIN record and the vehicle's current configuration. If a previous replacement used a different engine variant, we identify it and ensure any future work uses the correct components.

items.q: How long does engine matching take?
items.a: VIN decoding and registration lookup take a few minutes. Cross-referencing manufacturer catalogues and physical verification typically takes around 1-2 hours for a full match. This is included as part of the rebuild or replacement process.

items.q: Do you match engines for M models and performance variants?
items.a: Yes. M-division engines (S-code) are distinct from their standard counterparts and we match them with the same VIN-first process. We handle M2, M3, M4, M5, M6, M8, X3 M, X4 M, X5 M, and X6 M engines.

items.q: What happens if the engine number doesn't match the VIN record?
items.a: If the engine number doesn't match the VIN record, we investigate why. The vehicle may have had a previous engine change, or the registration records may be incorrect. We work with you to confirm the correct specification before any work begins.
